JOHN O'NEILL, 39. Decision.

SUPREME COURT OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK, COUNTY OF NEW YORK. 

Plaintiff,

Solicitor of the High Court of 

Justice of Northern Ireland. against

PILGRIM SAVINGS BANK and ARTHUR FARRELL, Defendants.

The issues in the above-entitled action having duly come on to be heard before this court without a jury, at a Special Term, Part VI thereof, held at the County Court House, in the Borough of

FORMS. 

Manhattan, City of New York, on the 19th day of April, 1931, and the plaintiff having appeared therein by his attorney, George Ridgeway, and the defendant Pilgrim Savings Bank, by its attorney, Richard O'Connor, and it further appearing that the defendant Arthur Farrell was duly served with a copy of the Summons and Complaint herein by publication, pursuant to an order of this court dated October 22, 1930, and that said defendant has failed to appear or plead in the action and that his time to do so has expired and the allegations and proofs of the parties having been heard, I do hereby find and decide as follows:

FINDINGS OF FACT. 

1. That at all the times hereinafter mentioned the defendant 

Pilgrim Savings Bank was and still is a domestic banking corporation, organized and existing under the laws of the State of New 

York, and having an office at No. 100 Chambers street, Borough of

Manhattan, New York City. 

2. That on the 15th day of November, 1925, Katherine Farrell opened an account in her name with the defendant Pilgrim Savings 

Bank, and had issued to her its bank book No. 500742. 

3. That after the opening of the said account by Katherine Farrell, she from time to time deposited sums of money in the account and the total of these sums with accrued interest thereon now amounts to $2,400.00, which is on deposit with the defendant Pilgrim 

Savings Bank to the credit of the account of "Katherine Farrell in trust for brother John O'Neill.' 

4. That on or about the twenty-fifth day of July, 1928, Katherine 

Farrell delivered the bank book No. 500742 of the Pilgrim Savings 

Bank to the plaintiff, John O'Neill. 

5. That on March 23, 1929, Katherine Farrell died intestate, a resident of Drumkeeragh, County Down, Ireland, and no administrator or other representative has ever been appointed of her estate. 

6. That on the said 23rd day of March, 1929, the date of Katherine Farrell's death, the bank book No. 500742 of the Pilgrim Savings Bank, was and now is in the possession of the plaintiff. 

7. That plaintiff demanded of the defendant Pilgrim Savings

Bank, payment of the monies standing to the credit of the account, evidenced by bank book No. 500742, but payment has never been received by him. 

8. That during her life time Katherine Farrell created a trust for the benefit of the plaintiff, John O'Neill, of the monies standing to the credit of the account in the name of "Katherine Farrell in trust for brother John O'Neill," evidenced by bank book of the Pilgrim 

Savings Bank, No. 500742. 

9. That said trust became absolute and irrevocable during the life time of Katherine Farrell, and the monies constituting the trust fund are the property of the plaintiff, John O'Neill. 

10. That the defendant, Arthur Farrell, has no right to or interest in the said fund consisting of the monies in the account in the name of "Katherine Farrell in trust for brother John O'Neill" evidenced by bank book of the Pilgrim Savings Bank, No. 500742.

FORMS. 

979 

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW. 

1. That plaintiff is entitled to judgment as follows: (a) That a trust in the said sum of $2,400.00, evidenced by bank book of the Pilgrim Savings Bank, No. 500742, was created by Katherine Farrell for the benefit of the plaintiff, John O'Neill, which became irrevocable during her life time and the said trust fund is now the property of the plaintiff. (b) That the defendant Arthur Farrell has no right or title thereto, and that he be excluded from any interest in or to the said account. (c) That the defendant Pilgrim Savings Bank be directed to pay to the plaintiff the sum of $2,400.00 now standing to the credit of the account in the name of "Katherine Farrell in trust for brother John 

O'Neill', evidenced by its bank book No. 500742. 

I direct judgment accordingly.

Dated: New York, April 28, 1931. 

PHOENIX INGRAHAM, Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of New York. 

40. Judgment.

At a Special Term, Part VI, of the Supreme Court, held in and for the County of New York, at the 

County Court House, in the Borough of Man hattan, City of New York, on the 28th day of 

April, 1931.

Present: HON. PHOENIX INGRAHAM, Justice. 

JOHN O'NEILL, Plaintiff, against

The issues in the above action having duly come on to be heard before Mr. Justice Phoenix Ingraham, without a jury, at a Special

Term, Part VI, of this court, held at the County Court House, in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, on the 19th day of

April, 1931, and the plaintiff having appeared therein by his attorney, George Ridgeway, and the defendant Pilgrim Savings Bank by 

Richard O'Connor its attorney, and the defendant Arthur Farrell having been duly served with a copy of the Summons and Complaint herein by publication, pursuant to an order of this court dated October 22, 1930, and the said defendant having failed to appear or plead in the action and his time so to do having expired and the

FORMS. 

issues having been duly tried and the court after due deliberation having made its decision on the 28th day of April, 1931, stating the facts found and the conclusions of law thereon, and directing judgment as hereinafter provided, it is, ON MOTION of George Ridgeway, attorney for the plaintiff,

ORDERED AND ADJUDGED as follows: 

I. That a trust in the sum of $2,400.00, evidenced by bank book of the Pilgrim Savings Bank, No. 500742, was created by Katherine

Farrell for the benefit of the plaintiff John O'Neill, which became irrevocable during her life time and the said trust fund is now the property of the plaintiff. 

II. That the defendant Arthur Farrell has no right or title thereto and is excluded from any interest in or to said account. 

III. That the defendant Pilgrim Savings Bank be and it hereby is directed to pay to the plaintiff the sum of $2,400.00 now standing to the credit of the account in the name of "Katherine Farrell in trust for brother John O'Neill", evidenced by its bank book No. 500742.

Enter, P. I.,

Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of New York.

DANIEL E. FINN, Clerk.
